dish: Friday couscous, moussaka and bourak at the lunch counter
w: Lower State Street's homegrown lunch counter since 1996 — Algerian founder Faisal Belakhdar still helps make the weekly specials (Badger Herald 2025); 'one of the best homegrown restaurants left on lower State Street' (Isthmus).

dish: A game-day beer in Regent Street's biggest beer garden
w: The Camp Randall pre-game fixture with Regent Street's largest outdoor beer garden — City Cast Madison's tailgate pick; OnMilwaukee's Madison sports-bar guide; Madison Magazine's Regent St game-day story.

dish: House beer from the 10-barrel brewhouse in a converted 1930s auto garage
w: Regent Street brewpub in a former auto-repair garage, brewhouse run by veteran brewer Grant Johnston (Isthmus); its event hall is 'custom-made for big Badger gameday tailgaters' (City Cast Madison).

dish: Red-sauce spaghetti and meatballs, or bialys and latkes from the deli side
w: Sam Brown's 2023 love letter to the old Greenbush 'Spaghetti Corners' — Italian red sauce plus Jewish deli (Madison Magazine, City Cast Madison); its blocked-off lot is the 'serious tailgater' party on game days (Isthmus).

address: 300 block of State St, Madison, WI 53703
w: Opened 1986 by Bishnu and Krishna Pradhan — billed as the first Nepali restaurant in the U.S.; closed for good in December 2025 (Daily Cardinal, Jan 2026). Kept, flagged.

dish: Fish-sauce-free curries and noodles, voted Best of Madison since 1997
w: Madison's long-running Thai standard-bearer — an Isthmus readers' Mad Faves Thai pick and a perennial Madison Magazine Best of Madison winner.

dish: Weekend brunch or the vegetable plates on the indoor-outdoor bar patio
w: Monroe Street's sunny California-style room where 'vegetables are the star' (Cap Times review); Travel Wisconsin-listed; rated 4.4 on ~900 reviews.

dish: Fish pakora and lamb shahi korma (lunch buffet)
address: 707 N High Point Rd, Madison, WI 53717
w: Madison Magazine Best of Madison 2024 South Asian gold; a top reader pick in the Cap Times' best strip-mall restaurants round-up.

dish: Hand-mixed Nürnberger bratwurst and Weisswurst, plus imported German groceries
w: Founded 1961 by Bavarian master sausage maker Fred Voll, who introduced Madison to its 'first bratwurst' (Fitchburg Historical Society); Travel Wisconsin-listed.

dish: German-style lagers on the Military Ridge Trail
w: German-tavern brewpub on Verona's Main Street beside the Military Ridge State Trail (Isthmus, Verona Press); grew into a second Fitchburg brewery.
Downtown Middleton's gelato café run by the Lumani brothers (Isthmus profile); Visit Middleton's dessert-guide staple.

dish: Butter-chicken pizza and masala eggplant parm
w: Two-kitchen Indian–Italian fusion (Cap Times: 'Indian spins on Italian dishes slap'); City Cast Madison's weird-pizza pick; ~200 butter-chicken pizzas a day (Badger Herald, mixed review).

dish: (closed) tenderloin filet and lake perch at the Yahara mouth
w: The von Rutenberg family's supper club on Lake Mendota since 1966 — 'one of Madison's best supper clubs for 59 years' — closed Aug. 29, 2025 (Cap Times). Kept, flagged.

dish: Small-batch cider from 18 area orchards, with house-made sausages
w: Mount Horeb cidery-restaurant pressing only locally grown apples, two-thirds of its kitchen sourced from Wisconsin farms (Isthmus, Brava); Travel Wisconsin-listed.

dish: The Reuben in the snug, with an Irish whiskey
w: Irish-born Peter McElvanna's Capitol Square gastropub (2010) uniting 'Irish and Midwestern flavors' (Isthmus); Destination Madison-listed.

Downtown Madison's decades-old pizza house, forced out of its W. Wilson St building for the final time (Cap Times: 'a sad end to Paisan's pizza'); Madison Magazine and On Wisconsin profiled it. Kept, flagged.

dish: A tour of the 1845 brewery and its brewery-memorabilia museum
w: The Midwest's oldest brewery (1845, ex-Joseph Huber) and the second-oldest in the U.S. (Wikipedia, Tasting Table); State Trunk Tour attraction pick.

dish: Friday fried cod or Great Lakes bluegill, clam pizza and chowder
w: Sardine chefs Phillip Hurley and John Gadau's Monroe Street fish house–meets–Wisconsin tavern (opened 2012; Wisconsin State Journal); one of Travel Wisconsin's 8 Madison fish-fry picks; a Cap Times family-dining favourite.
